subject: general
question: A user wants to have a bulleted list in MS PowerPoint. After typing a list item and pressing Enter, they want to create a sub-bullet point (a lower-level bullet). Which of the following actions will reliably achieve this?

options.text: Clicking the 'Decrease List Level' button in the Paragraph group
Clicking the 'Increase List Level' button in the Paragraph group

solution:
The correct answer is __**Clicking the 'Increase List Level' button in the Paragraph group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In MS PowerPoint, to create a sub-bullet point (lower-level bullet), the 'Increase List Level' button is used, located in the **Paragraph group** of the Home tab.
 
• This action indents the selected bullet point, making it a sub-bullet under the previous higher-level bullet.
 
• The 'Increase List Level' button serves as a reliable and user-friendly method for managing hierarchical bullet points.
 
• Alternatively, you can also use the **Tab key** on your keyboard to achieve the same effect while working with bullet lists.
 
• The functionality of the 'Increase List Level' button helps in structuring content logically and improving presentation clarity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paragraph Group:**

 
 
• Located on the Home tab in MS PowerPoint, the Paragraph group includes tools for managing text alignment, bullets, numbering, and indentation.
 
• The 'Increase List Level' and 'Decrease List Level' buttons are part of this group.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts:**
 
 
• For creating sub-bullets, you can use the **Tab key**.
 
• To move a sub-bullet back to a higher level, press **Shift + Tab**.
 
 
 
• **Bullet Points:**
 
 
• Bullet points are used to organize content into a list format for better readability and understanding.
 
• They can be hierarchical, with main bullets and sub-bullets indicating different levels of importance.
 
 
 
• **Sub-Bullets:**
 
 
• Sub-bullets are used to provide additional details or examples related to a main point.
 
• The indentation visually distinguishes sub-bullets from main bullets.
 
 
 
• **Indentation in Presentations:**
 
 
• Indentation plays a crucial role in structuring content in presentations, ensuring a logical flow of information.
 
• Proper use of indentation and bullet hierarchy can make presentations more engaging and easier to follow.
